The task is to act as a skeptical but fair reader and compare the book with the strongest specific alternative explanation for the term "Righteousness". I must return only the requested structured res...{
  "book_core": "Righteousness is right-living: the doing of God's commandments, kept as the garment of righteous acts; God is Right-Living by definition, and even complete obedience earns no wage because it is only duty; righteousness is given by grace but never renames wrong-living right.",
  "book 2nd": "Garment imagery (fine linen = righteous acts); Romans 4 excludes wage-work, not obedience; 1 John 3:7; Deut 6:25; Ps 119:172; Luke 17 servant parable; Phil 3:9; Heb 11:8; garments 43 chapter.",
  "strongest_counter": "Forensic/imputed righteousness: a legal declaration in which Christ's righteousness is credited to the believer's account (classic Reformation/Protestant reading of justification).",
  "counter_basis": [
    "Romans 4:3-8",
    "Romans 5:17 19",
    "2 Corinthians 5:21",
    "Philippians 3:9"
  ],
  "comparison": "The book supplies stronger explanatory power for the garment imagery (Rev 19:8 dikaiomata = righteous acts), the explicit equation of righteousness with commandment-keeping (Deut 6 25; Ps 119:172), and 1 John 3:7. It also accounts for the wedding-garment parable and the distinction between wage-work and obedience (Luke 17). The counter reading treats the garment as Christ's imputed status rather than the believer's own righteous acts and struggles to integrate the OT definitions of righteousness as doing the law. The book's wage/obedience distinction aligns with the prior finding on works and avoids contradiction with Phil 3:9 by locating the contrast in source rather than substance. Therefore the book's core identification accounts for the supplied scriptural evidence better overall.

  "rationale": "The book's core identification of righteousness as right-living (the doing of God's commandments, worn as the garment of righteous acts) best accounts for the full range of the supplied texts once the prior findings on faith (trust held steady through obedience), belief (submission to the word), love (commandment-keeping), and works (deeds that become obedience when they execute God's command, distinct from wage-labor) are treated as established. The chapter's derivation from the wedding garment, Revelation 19:8 (dikaiōmata as righteous acts), Deuteronomy 6:25, Psalm 119:172, and 1 John 3:7 is direct and uniform; Romans 4 is handled without contradiction by excluding only wage-work that would put God in debt (Luke 17:7-10), not obedience itself.   "book_core_identification": "Righteousness is right-living: for those under God's authority, the doing of His commandments (the law kept and worn as the garment of righteous acts).",
  "book_secondary_elaborations": [
    "God Himself is Right-Living by definition—His ways and works are the measure of right (Deut 32:4; Ps 145:17).",
    "The fine linen of Revelation 19:8 is the plural righteous acts (dikaiōmata) of the saints, given yet arrayed by them.",
    "Romans 4 excludes only wage-work that would create debt, not obedience; complete obedience earns no wage because the servant has only done his duty (Luke 17:7-10).",
    "Righteousness is given and reckoned by grace, yet the gift never renames wrong-living right; faith is counted for righteousness precisely as the obedient trust that does the word (Heb 11:8; prior findings on faith and belief).",
    "Philippians 3:9 contrasts source and claim (mine by debt vs. of God by faith), not right-living against lawlessness; the walk continues by the same rule.",
    "The garment symbol unifies the whole: covenant covering restored, washed when soiled, kept by continued right-living (Isa 61:10; Zech 3; John 13; Rev 3:4; 16:15)."
  ],
  "strongest_counter_interpretation": "Righteousness is primarily the forensic/legal status of right standing before God, the righteousness of God (or of Christ) imputed/credited to the believer through faith alone, symbolized as a clean robe that covers the sinner; ethical right-living is a secondary fruit or evidence that flows from that status rather than the identity of righteousness itself.",

  "counter_relation_to_book_core": "CONTRADICTS",

    "Romans 3:21-26; 4:3-8 and Philippians 3:9 present righteousness as God's gift apart from works, credited to faith, justifying the ungodly—classic forensic language.",

    "Traditional Protestant consensus and the New Perspective alternatives still center right standing or covenant membership over the act of commandment-keeping as the primary lexical identity."

  "book_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Directly accounts for the definitional OT statements (Deut 6:25; Ps 119:172; Deut 32:4; Ps 145:17) and 1 John 3:7 without demotion or redefinition.",

    "Integrates Romans 4 via the wage/obedience distinction already established in the works prior finding and Luke 17:7-10; faith is counted precisely because it is the obedient trust of the prior faith finding.",
    "Unifies the garment symbol across Genesis 3, Isaiah 61, Ezekiel 16, Zechariah 3, John 13, and Revelation without collapsing sanctification into a mere status or treating obedience as optional.",

    "Strong surface fit with the 'apart from works' / 'counted for righteousness' phrasing in Romans 4 and Philippians 3:9 when those texts are isolated from the rest of the canon.",
    "Matches the historic Protestant emphasis on imputation and the symbolic use of robes as covering.",
    "Avoids any appearance of works-righteousness that might seem to compromise sola fide."
  ],
